about.headline: I build reliable backend systems that are clear to operate and ready for production.
paragraphs: I'm an early-career backend engineer with production experience building Go microservices, asynchronous processing systems, cloud integrations, and operational tooling.

My work has taken me from API and database design to weekly releases, monitoring, on-call support, and incident investigation. I care about performance, recovery, observability, and the small engineering decisions that make services dependable.

highlights: Developed production Go microservices across cloud-resource management, FinOps, notifications, and observability.
Built Redis-backed asynchronous workers, REST APIs, MySQL workflows, and AWS integrations.
Executed weekly releases, joined 24-hour on-call rotations, and investigated 30+ production issues.
Improved API performance through pagination, SQL optimization, indexing, and batched retrieval.

projects.title: JD Lens
projects.description: Built a browser extension that displays the most useful details from a LinkedIn job post in a floating panel, removing the need to repeatedly expand and scan the full description.
details: Extracts and summarizes the role, company, location, required experience, and preferred skills directly from the active job page.
Presents the information in a compact floating panel so users can evaluate opportunities faster while browsing LinkedIn.
Uses a platform-adapter architecture so support for additional job sites can be added without rewriting the shared parsing and presentation logic.

projects.title: Database-level cost attribution
projects.description: Built a scheduled system that estimated each database's share of a common RDS bill using storage, CPU, and memory weights. It helped a client identify unused databases and contributed to an approximately 70% month-over-month cost reduction.
details: Designed a weighted attribution model using database storage, CPU, and memory consumption.
Automated scheduled collection and calculation across shared AWS RDS infrastructure.
Made database-level costs visible so unused resources could be identified and removed.

projects.title: Sequential transition engine
projects.description: Created restart-resilient Redis workers that preserved one-at-a-time ordering within 100+ resource groups while allowing five workers to process different groups concurrently.
details: Preserved strict sequential execution for operations belonging to the same resource group.
Allowed independent groups to be processed concurrently across five workers.
Designed recovery behavior so queued work could safely continue after restarts.

projects.title: Multi-channel notification service
projects.description: Built an end-to-end service for Slack, email, Google Chat, and Microsoft Teams with queued dispatch, templates, throttling, actionable messages, and delayed failure retry.
details: Created a common delivery workflow across Slack, email, Google Chat, and Microsoft Teams.
Added templates, throttling, actionable messages, and queued asynchronous dispatch.
Handled transient delivery failures through delayed retry processing.

projects.title: Text-to-SQL with T5
projects.description: Fine-tuned a T5 model to translate natural-language questions into basic to moderately complex SQL queries. The research was later published as a technical book chapter.
details: Fine-tuned a T5 transformer model on natural-language and SQL query pairs.
Evaluated generation across basic and moderately complex query structures.
Developed the work into research that was published as a technical book chapter.
